title: larrea tridentata subsp. glutinosa
intro: Larrea tridentata subsp. glutinosa, commonly known as creosotebush, is a shrub-like plant native to the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. It has been used in traditional medicine for its numerous health benefits, which include its potential to reduce inflammation, improve immune function, and exhibit antimicrobial and antiviral properties. The therapeutic actions of creosotebush are attributed to its bioactive constituents, such as phenolic compounds, flavonoids, and triterpenoids, which have been shown to exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory activities. Additionally, creosotebush has been traditionally used to treat various health conditions, including fever, cough, and digestive issues, although further research is needed to confirm its efficacy and safety for human use.
